utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone after a relatively long period of not sitting. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Defence would like to raise a preliminary matter. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, you are right. We have to address Your Honours on the issue of our ability to continue with the trial, and I will read short statement in B/C/S. [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are addressing you after our return from the field and after a month during which there was no sessions, and the Defence has been given that time to prepare for the Tomasica Prosecutor's case. The reason we are addressing you is our duty to inform you that the Defence has not succeeded in such a short time to prepare for the continuation of this case with regard to Tomasica. The Defence wants to officially file on the record that the time that has been given to us to prepare for the Tomasica segment was neither reasonable nor sufficient to allow the Defence to complete all the preparatory actions which are necessary to adequately and fully confront and refute the testimonies of the Prosecutor's expert witnesses. Despite our great effort, the number of expert witnesses and their various specialities have not allowed us to have a complete overview of their testimonies despite our consultations with the Defence expert witnesses. [In English] I think that the translation is a bit different. It says "despite consultations with the Defence expert witnesses." We did not have consultations with Defence expert witnesses. [Interpretation] Despite the efforts of -- invested by the Defence, the allocated time has not allowed us to find Defence expert witnesses. Even if we had, that would not have been enough for the expert witnesses to review all the materials provided by the Prosecutor's expert witnesses and to prepare for the cross-examination. The facts in this case say that the Tomasica investigations started in 2002. They continued in 2004 and in 2006 with the help of the prosecutor's office of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The final works on the exhumation of the bodies finished in 2013. We can find this fact in paragraph 2 of Ian Hanson's paper. Let us mention that the entire ICMP was involved in this work, the ICMP being the International Commission on Missing Persons. The Prosecutor had the help from the police and the prosecutor's office of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Obviously, this was what involved a lot of work and the Prosecutor needed more than a decade to complete it with the help of a vast machinery that it had at its disposal. The Defence could not complete the work with the limited resources and the limited number of people that were -- that were allocated to us in just a month. We take this opportunity to ask for -- from the Trial Chamber to allocate us additional time to prepare and to continue to work professionally and to protect the rights of our client. The Defence is prepared to cross-examine the fact witnesses provided by the Prosecutor. As far as the Prosecutor's investigation is concerned, we can tell you that it is ongoing. Last night we received new information that the Prosecutor learned in their conversation with the witness who is supposed to testify second in this case, so it is obvious that the Defence needs additional time to be able to cross-examine the Prosecutor's witnesses. Thank you for having listened to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just very briefly and just about one aspect of the argument raised by Mr. Lukic. First I should note that we had no indication before this morning immediately before we commenced that he would be offering that position to the Court; but, in any event, I feel at least compelled to point out one aspect of the argument that may illustrate the larger fallacy in his position, and that is the claim that somehow the initiation and unsuccessful efforts to probe Tomasica initially in 2002 and then only the partially successful efforts to excavate that large site in 2004 and 2006 and then eventually the probing and identification of additional remains resulting in the excavation in 2013 are somehow part of an ongoing process that bears some relationship to the amount of time that must be invested by the Defence in analysing the results of the 2013 excavation and exhumations. There are few more striking examples of the apples-and-oranges fallacy that I can think of. These are two completely different things. And the fact that there a was an unsuccessful probe in 2002 and then there was a long gap between that time and the 2013 excavation have absolutely nothing to do with the review of the very concise, very clear information about the 2013 exhumation that was adduced in response to those efforts and that has been presented to the Defence. That is aside from the issue of when the Defence was properly seized of the information about the Tomasica excavation such that efforts to identify experts who could assist in their evaluative efforts might first be commenced. So I cannot offer an exhaustive review of Mr. Lukic's comments, but I would suggest that these two issues alone suffice to make clear that this submission is misplaced and should not result in the relief sought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, anything to add? Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise. Just to very briefly add to Mr. Tieger remarks, having been involved with the fact witnesses. Mr. Lukic suggested on the basis of having received a proofing note yesterday that that meant investigations were continuing. Of course, he received the standard sort of information that both parties have provided during the course of witness preparation, and I think to misconstrue that to suggest that there remain some sort of investigative process beyond the standard witness preparation is misleading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am afraid that I cannot agree with my learned friend that I was misconstruing anything. The documents were offered to this witness to comment on them yesterday. At least we were informed that way. So he never commented on the documents mentioned in that proofing note, never before. So it was part of the investigation. You will probably be offered this chart made from that conversation, and you will see from the information report that many things were raised for the first time, and we can ask the witness if those facts were actually raised with him for the first time yesterday. So I'm not misconstruing anything. It's visible from the documents that the Prosecution was conducting investigation yesterday with that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything else, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber noted that the Defence declared its preparedness to cross-examine at least the witnesses of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, that's the reason why we'll not at this very moment determine the matter. We'll further consider it and we'll also keep in the back of our minds, Mr. Lukic, that the matter of the time to be granted to prepare for the reopening has been litigated and has resulted in a decision by the Appeals Chamber in which the appeal against the decision of this Trial Chamber was denied, but we'll look at all that together and not hasten and hurry at this moment to give a decision within half an hour. We'll take at least one or two days to further consider the matter. Any other matter you intended to raise, Mr. Lukic, or was this the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you. That's all we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to say that it's not enough in no way. Then we briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll take a break. During the break, the Chamber will consider the arguments raised by the parties in relation to protective measures and we'll give our decision upon return, which will be at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has heard the submissions in relation -- and the request for protective measures for Witness RM383 and has decided to grant the protective measure as requested; that is, face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym. The reasons will be given soon. Could we turn into closed session in order to allow the witness to enter the courtroom, and immediately after he has taken his seat we'll proceed in open session though with these protective measures.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Witness, you'll first be examined by Mr. Traldi. You find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is, as I told you before, is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning again, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now could we please have 65 ter 32659, not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, what you should see on your screen now is a pseudonym sheet which will have your name, your date of birth, and your pseudonym in this trial. Please don't read any of the information out loud. But if it correctly reflects the information I just mentioned just now, if you could please affirm that for the record by saying "yes."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this be admitted into evidence as the next confidential Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7415, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7415 is admitted, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we now have 65 ter 31081, not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, did you give a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2014?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor during an interview conducted in the year 2014?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to the right side of the screen, the English version, do you recognise the signature in the bottom right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can I ask that the court officer call up page 6 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, page 1 gives a wrong date, at least an incomprehensible date for the interview. 201 is not a year. Could that be corrected. And let's now move to page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, do you see on the right side of the page next to the word "potpis," do you see a signature again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Whose is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we go for a moment into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, did you have an opportunity to review your statement in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's -- there was B/C/S on the English channel. There still is, but now I think it has been repaired. If you put your next question to the witness, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to read your statement this weekend and make any corrections you wished to make?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Aside from the correction we discussed a moment ago, if I were to ask you questions similar to those you were asked in the taking of your statement, would you give the same answers, in substance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would give the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And now that you've taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the truthfulness and accuracy of the information you've provided in this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 31081, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7416, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7416 is admitted, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will now provide a very brief summary of the witness's evidence. I've explained to him that it is for the public and not part of his evidence and confirmed with him that the limited information contained therein will not give rise to his security concerns. RM383 gives evidence about one instance of the collection, transport, and burial in the Tomasica mass grave of persons killed in Prijedor municipality. And I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Before I do, I'd tender as well the limited map book that we have made associated with the Tomasica reopening, 65 ter 32662.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Court Officer has hard copies for Your Honours, and the Defence has been provided a hard copy this morning. We'd propose it be admitted on the same basis as the municipalities and Sarajevo map books, and I've been told that with that understanding the Defence has no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that any markings or whatever are not -- not accepted by -- not objecting to the admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the Chamber would like to receive those copies, hard copies. Mr. Stojanovic, you received a copy already?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honours. We received it earlier today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, and I do understand there's no objection against having it admitted into evidence but that that does not mean that you do not challenge any of the markings, the layout. Whatever interpretation could be given to that, you'll keep your hands free in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, number to be assigned to the Tomasica court binder.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Which is 65 ter number 32662 is Exhibit P7417, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Mr. Traldi, I saw that there are some -- even some signatures. Any reason to have it partly under seal or not at all? Because I don't know whose they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could put it tentatively under seal and I'll come back to Your Honours within the next hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Provisionally it's put under seal. And I'm mainly focusing, for example, at pages 3 and 4. Yes, provisionally under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please repeat the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 32662, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we move into private session briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you now about when you were at the site itself. Without mentioning how you got there or where you came there from, can you just tell us what it was like when you got to the grave-site the first time, what you were able to see, hear, and smell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw some earth that had been dug up near the grave, and I saw an excavator.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) The soldiers unloaded the bodies into the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the last time you were at the site before you left, were you or anyone there at the time instructed to close the grave, to put all the disturbed earth back in and cover it up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one said anything. While we were there, there was no one else at the location except for the group that had brought the corpses and unloaded them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And are you aware of any discussion with members of your group about closing the site, covering it up, filling the pit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, we did speak among ourselves, but we couldn't make any decisions. No one asked us anything. The superiors were supposed to be involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did any of those superiors ever issue an instruction to close the site to anyone in your group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my examination. I'd ask that we very briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before I give an opportunity to the Defence to cross-examine the witness, Judge Fluegge would have one or more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, you said in answering a question of Mr. Traldi that "the superiors were supposed to be involved in that." Who were your superiors you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had in mind those who were responsible, those who were more senior in terms of rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To which institution did they belong?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt. If we might address that in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's a good session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Rather than to start with the next witness I'd like to deal with a few procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I might deal with one leftover from this morning that I'd undertaken to get back to the Chamber about, P7417, the Tomasica court binder. I've been assured by my colleagues that it can be a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can be a public exhibit. Therefore, P7417 which was provisionally put under seal is now a public exhibit. I'd like to deal with a few matters. The first deals with the request to replace the current the e-court version of P2508. On the 9th of December, 2013, document bearing Rule 65 ter number 2382a was admitted into evidence as Exhibit P2508, and I refer to transcript page 20453. On the 7th of April of this year, the Prosecution, following an informal agreement with the Defence, requested via an e-mail that the Chamber replace the current version of Exhibit P2508 with the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 2382b. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the current version of P2508 in e-court with the new version. I move one further down in my agenda in order to avoid that we have to move into and then again out of private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the next item deals with comment chart for Witness RM382. On the 15th of June of this year, the Prosecution requested the Chamber's leave via e-mail to use a comment chart for five to ten documents to be used with Witness RM382. The Chamber granted this request on the 18th of June and informed the parties of its decision, and this decision is hereby put on the record. And the next item addresses the Defence. The Defence has indicated that it intends could call a number of its witnesses pursuant to Rule 92 bis, and the Chamber wonders whether the Defence could indicate when it will file its Rule 92 bis motions. Mr. Lukic, when do you think you could respond to this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You really caught me by surprise, although probably we'll have it already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the reason why I give you time to find out. Later this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe it would be a good idea to have a weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A weekend. Okay. Then we'll hear from you not later than --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Monday. That's fine. That would be Monday, the 29th of June. The next item deals with the verification of translation of documents bearing 65 ter numbers 19777, and the admission of document bearing 65 ter number 19777e. During the testimony of Nenad Davidovic on the 11th and the 12th of February of this year, the Chamber invited the Prosecution to seek verification from CLSS of the translation of the pages 13 and 22 of document bearing 65 ter number 19777, which is the witness's diary. I refer to transcript pages 31.610 and 31.579. On the 26th of February, the Prosecution advised the Chamber via an e-mail on the translation of the word "ljekara" on page 22 and advised that the corrected page 13 forms part of an excerpt of the diary which has been uploaded under 65 ter number 19777e. Perhaps I spell the word "ljekara" because my pronunciation may be wrong. It's l-j-e-k-a-r-k. Yes, the last -- it ends last three -- last four letters are k-a-r-a. Yes, there we are. The Chamber requested the Prosecution file this e-mail. On the 29th of March, the Defence advised the Chamber via an e-mail that it has no objection to the admission of the excerpt and the Chamber hereby admits the document bearing 65 ter number 19777e into evidence. And, Mr. Registrar, you're invited to assign an exhibit number for that 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will be Exhibit D1081, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it a D number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, I stand corrected. It's P7418.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7418 is admitted into evidence. I deal with one final matter; that is, the clarification on the status of Exhibit P7198. On the 22nd of May of this year, P7198, an intercept, was admitted into evidence and placed under seal. The Trial Chamber notes that the Prosecution did not request P7198 to be placed under seal, but that most of the submissions and filings relating to this document were confidential. The Chamber considers that the status of P7198 should be public and wonders whether there's any objections from the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not off the top of my head, Your Honour, but we can discuss it overnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the same question to the Defence, but if we hear from you tomorrow or the day after tomorrow, then we can give further instructions to the Registry about the confidential status of P7198. I leave it to that for the time being. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 23rd of June, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of June, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.14 p.m.,
